body:
Ross wrote:

>"Aren't you the one who was arguing that society couldn't accomodate
>different,
>sensitive types like TK?  Just think of 
>leftists as special people and then afford
>them the same latitude as you'd have society afford TK."
>

Pyro replied:

>White liberals are out to keep everyone from thinking and speaking freely. 
>Their destruction is therefore justified. 
>

Pyro, your argument doesn't follow. How did you reach your conclusion? Ross
made an excellent point.

However, if we follow your reasoning, what does the following quote say about
TK's desire for "everyone" to think and speak freely, and what should our
response be? "But even if most people in industrial-technological society were
well satisfied, we (FC) would still be opposed to that form of society..."
para. 86. And TK advocates revolution in various other paragraphs.

BTW, I usually emphasize the positive aspects of the manifesto, but arguments
like yours would make a devil's advocate of any of TK's moderate supporters -
and there are a lot of us. Is that your goal? Do you also wish to alienate
others who might be brought to appreciate the manifesto through such hostile
stances? TK warned against this.

Consider this quote from para. 191: "One should think twice before encouraging
any other social conflict than that between the power-holding elite (which
wields technology) and the general public (over which technology exerts its
power)."  Do you suppose the liberals you despise so much are the *real* power
holding elite? I think you are mistaken there.

"('We live in a world in which relatively few people - maybe 500 or 1,000 -
make the important decisions' - Philip B. Heymann of Harvard Law School, quoted
by Anthony Lewis, New York Times, April 21, 1995.)" Quoted by TK in ISAIF,
paragraph 67.

-Susan
